question: Two trains having lengths of 100 m and 500 m are running at speeds of 100 km/hr and 110 km/hr, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same direction) = 110 − 100 = 10 km/hr.

**Total Distance** = Sum of lengths = 100 + 500 = 600 m = 0.6 km.

**Time (hours)** = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 0.6 ÷ 10 = 0.06 hours.

**Time (minutes)** = 0.06 × 60 = 3.6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/640d848e2e71d4bb7a7a12170f19844a7305a5491838912c6db9ad983b355351.png] 

**Given:**

Length of train 1 (L₁) = 100 m

Length of train 2 (L₂) = 500 m

Speed of train 1 (S₁) = 100 km/hr

Speed of train 2 (S₂) = 110 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 100 + 500 = 600 m

⇒ Relative Speed = S₂ − S₁ = 110 − 100 = 10 km/hr

⇒ Convert Speed to m/sec: 10 × (5/18) = 50/18 m/sec

⇒ Time (sec) = 600 ÷ (50/18) = (600 × 18) ÷ 50 = 12 × 18 = 216 seconds

⇒ Time (min) = 216 ÷ 60 = 3.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed is the **difference** (S₁ − S₂). If they move in **opposite directions**, it is the **sum** (S₁ + S₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses another train or a bridge, the **total distance** is always the **sum of their lengths**.</p
